global_rules.rule: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.
Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.
Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.
You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
Complete each task in a logical, and efficient execution flow.
Access rights are defined by roles and grant granular control across tables.
To log any issue/interrupted service, create an Incident record.
Mandatory Inputs: opened_by (user submitting), caller_id (user affected), short_description, impact, and urgency.
Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
All new Incidents are set to status = new.
assigned_to must be an active user with the Agent or Manager role and must be a member of the specified assignment_group.
Valid Status Transitions: new → in_progress / on_hold / resolved; in_progress → on_hold / resolved; on_hold → in_progress (Must log on_hold_reason before transition); resolved → closed / in_progress.
An Incident cannot transition to resolved without mandatory fields: resolution_code, and resolution_notes (free-form text, max 2000 chars).
The incidents that are in resolved status will transition to closed after 72 hours.
All changes must originate from a Change Request record.
All new Changes are set to status = new.
Change Types (Enumeration): standard (pre-approved, low risk), normal (requires planning/approval), emergency (requires immediate CAB approval override).
A Problem must be created when a recurring incident pattern or a major incident is identified.
The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.
All new Problems are set to status = new.
If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.
A Problem transitions to closed only after the permanent fix has been successfully implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.
Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
All IT assets must be recorded in the configuration_item table.
Only CIs with status = in_use or status = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in status = retired or status = disposed.
All CIs must have a recorded owner_id.
SLAs are automatically aligned based on priority linked to the incident.
Metrics tracked are limited to target_mins.

The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in stage = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.
If the SLA exceeds its duration (stage = breached), the escalation flag on the Incident must be set to true, and an automatic notification sent to the Manager.
Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.
When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.
All knowledge links must track used_as type: suggested, applied, or resolution.
Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.
Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.
All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.
403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).
409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.
Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

triage.name: Incident Triage
triage.src: 3.1. Incident Registration, 3.2. Incident Assignment, 6. Service Level Management (SLA), 7. Knowledge Management
steps: Validate mandatory inputs: opened_by, caller_id, short_description, impact, urgency. Stop if any missing.
Create Incident record with status = new.
Calculate priority automatically based on Impact x Urgency matrix.
Apply SLA based on calculated priority.
Search for relevant published Knowledge articles and link matching ones as used_as = suggested.
Assign incident: ensure assigned_to is an active Agent or Manager and member of assignment_group. Stop if assignment invalid.

incident.assignee: Agent or Manager based on assignment_group

housekeeping.name: Incident Closure and Data Integrity
housekeeping.src: 3.3. Incident Lifecycle and Closure, 8.1. Data Integrity Checks
steps: Verify incident is in resolved status for 72 hours before closing.
Ensure all mandatory dependencies are satisfied before closing any record.
Log all work with timestamp (created_on) and user_id.

priority.name: Incident and Problem Priority Matrix
levels: high: medium impact + high urgency OR high impact + medium urgency
moderate: low impact + high urgency OR medium impact + medium urgency OR high impact + low urgency
low: low impact + medium urgency OR medium impact + low urgency

escalation.name: SLA Breach Escalation
steps: If SLA stage becomes breached, set escalation flag on incident to true.
must_not: Pause SLA timer unless incident is on_hold with reason Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.

definitions.Incident: An unplanned interruption to an IT service or reduction in the quality of an IT service.
definitions.Service Request: A formal request from a user for something to be provided – for example, a request for information or advice.
definitions.Change Request: A formal proposal for a change to be made to an IT service or infrastructure.
definitions.Problem: A cause of one or more incidents. The cause is not usually known at the time a problem record is created.
definitions.Configuration Item (CI): Any component or asset that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service.
definitions.SLA: Service Level Agreement; a contract between an IT service provider and a customer that describes the service, documents service level targets, and specifies the responsibilities of both parties.
definitions.CAB: Change Advisory Board; a group of people that advises the change manager in the assessment, prioritization, and scheduling of changes.
definitions.CMDB: Configuration Management Database; a database used to store configuration records throughout their lifecycle.
